extracted.intended_audience: USPTO examiners; patent owners and patent practitioners preparing or responding to supplemental examination requests
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance on how the USPTO determines whether items of information in a supplemental examination request raise a substantial new question of patentability (SNQ), how to handle related litigation and factual corrections, and the required content of the supplemental examination certificate and accompanying reasons document.

rubrics_metrics.name: Three-month determination deadline
rubrics_metrics.description: Within three months after the filing date of a request for supplemental examination, the Office will determine whether a substantial new question of patentability affecting any claim of the patent is raised by any of the items of information presented in the request.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The determination will generally be based on the claims in effect at the time and become part of the official record. If the three-month period ends on a Saturday, Sunday, or federal holiday in D.C., the certificate should issue by the preceding business day. Examiners should take up the request roughly six weeks after filing and must complete the determination within the statutory three-month period.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scope of review limited to identified items and claims
rubrics_metrics.description: The determination will generally be limited to a review of the item(s) of information identified in the request as applied to the identified claim(s) of the patent.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the patent owner wants consideration of an item with respect to multiple claims, the request must identify each claim and include the required detailed explanation for each claim. The Office will generally not initiate supplemental examination for claims that were not requested.

rubrics_metrics.name: SNQ standard (substantial likelihood important to reasonable examiner)
rubrics_metrics.description: An item of information raises a substantial new question of patentability where there is a substantial likelihood that a reasonable examiner would consider the item of information important in deciding whether or not the claim is patentable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The SNQ standard in supplemental examination proceedings is identical to the SNQ standard in ex parte reexamination proceedings (see MPEP §2242). It is not necessary to establish a prima facie case of unpatentability for an SNQ to be present.

rubrics_metrics.name: SNQ preclusion by prior final decisions or earlier Office review
rubrics_metrics.description: An SNQ is not present if the same question of patentability has already been (A) decided in a final holding of invalidity by a federal court (after all appeals) as to the claim, (B) decided in an earlier concluded examination or review by the Office, or (C) raised to or by the Office in a pending reexamination or supplemental examination of the patent.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: ‘Earlier concluded examination or review’ includes original prosecution, reissue, earlier reexamination/supplemental examination, and concluded PTAB trials (post-grant, IPR, CBM). Issues involving 35 U.S.C. 325(d) must be referred to the Director of the CRU.

rubrics_metrics.name: Treatment of prior art previously considered (‘old art’)
rubrics_metrics.description: Prior art that was cited or considered by the Office (old art) does not necessarily preclude an SNQ; an SNQ may be based solely on old art when the old art is presented/viewed in a new light or in a different way with a material new argument or interpretation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Determinations are fact-specific and made case-by-case. The request should explain how the item(s) present the material new view or argument compared to earlier examinations or reviews.

rubrics_metrics.name: No requirement to show prima facie unpatentability
rubrics_metrics.description: It is not necessary that a prima facie case of unpatentability exist for an SNQ to be present as to a claim.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A claim could raise an SNQ even if the examiner would not necessarily reject it as anticipated or obvious based on the submitted items. Note that KSR does not alter the SNQ legal standard.

rubrics_metrics.name: Requirement for separate, detailed explanation for each claim (37 CFR 1.610(b)(5))
rubrics_metrics.description: The request must include a separate, detailed explanation of the relevance and manner of applying each item of information to each claim of the patent for which supplemental examination is requested.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the patent owner fails to explain how any item may be applied to a claim, the owner is not entitled to supplemental examination of that claim. A notice of a noncompliant request should be mailed where required. Example: request that only explains application to claims 1–5 but requests examination of claims 1–10 will not entitle determination for claims 6–10.

rubrics_metrics.name: Examiner discretion to analyze items across requested claims
rubrics_metrics.description: While the Office will generally analyze an item only with respect to the claim(s) identified by the patent owner, the examiner has the discretion to determine whether any of the items properly submitted raise an SNQ affecting any of the claims for which supplemental examination is requested.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The examiner may analyze items in a manner other than that provided by the patent owner, including considering multiple items against multiple claims. However, the patent owner is not entitled to a determination for claims lacking the required explanation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Effect of finding an SNQ — reexamination may be ordered
rubrics_metrics.description: If the examiner determines that an SNQ affecting a patent claim has been raised by at least one of the items, reexamination will be ordered under 35 U.S.C. 257.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Once reexamination is ordered, the Office may, in its sole discretion, reexamine claims other than those for which supplemental examination was requested (35 U.S.C. 303(a)). If claims are amended by a certificate or reissued patent after reexamination is ordered, reexamination should be on the basis of the claims as amended.

rubrics_metrics.name: Treatment of items limited to correction of factual information
rubrics_metrics.description: An item of information limited to correction of factual information alone (e.g., correction of a missing/erroneous foreign priority or domestic benefit claim, or correction of common ownership) generally will not raise an SNQ.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: To raise an SNQ, such factual corrections should be accompanied by one or more additional items (e.g., intervening references) that would cause patentability under 35 U.S.C. 102/103 to depend upon the corrected factual information. The Office recommends including additional items that could make patentability depend on the correction.

rubrics_metrics.name: Procedure for domestic benefit / priority corrections (example guidance)
rubrics_metrics.description: When a request includes a claim of missing domestic benefit plus an intervening reference, the examiner will first determine whether the intervening reference raises an SNQ if the effective filing date remains unchanged.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the reference would raise an SNQ absent correction, the examiner may preliminarily consider entitlement to the earlier filing date, but final entitlement generally is made in the resulting reexamination proceeding where appropriate amendments and petitions can be filed. If the intervening reference does not raise an SNQ, the domestic benefit correction will not be further considered on the merits.

rubrics_metrics.name: Handling when only factual correction information is provided
rubrics_metrics.description: If the only information in the request is correction of factual information that does not itself raise an SNQ, the supplemental examination certificate will state no SNQ is raised and the reasons will indicate that no additional items showing dependency of patentability on the corrected fact were included.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: a lone parent-patent copy and explanation showing claim support without an intervening reference will typically result in a conclusion that no SNQ is raised.

rubrics_metrics.name: Obligation to notify Office of federal court decisions and litigation search
rubrics_metrics.description: The patent owner must promptly notify the Office of any federal court decision involving the patent. Before determination, a litigation search by Technical Support Staff may be performed to check for litigation involvement.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If litigation is discovered or a federal court decision exists, the request must be brought to the attention of CRU SPRS or TC QAS to ensure actions conform to Office policy and guidelines. Guidance for additional litigation searches may be obtained from the Office of the Solicitor library when needed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Effect of federal court decisions on supplemental examination
rubrics_metrics.description: A non-final federal court decision concerning validity/unenforceability has no binding effect on the Office's determination of whether an SNQ exists; the Office will make its determination without awaiting court decisions. A final federal court decision (after all appeals) upholding invalidity or unenforceability is controlling on the Office and the Office will not examine claims finally held invalid or unenforceable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If claims requested to be examined have been finally held invalid or unenforceable, those claims will not be examined and the supplemental examination may be limited or not conducted. If a supplemental examination certificate inadvertently issued but a final holding of invalidity/unenforceability is brought to the Office's attention prior to the certificate's issuance, the certificate will be vacated; if the final holding occurs after electronic issuance to IFW/Patent Center, the certificate will not be vacated.

rubrics_metrics.name: Content of the Supplemental Examination Certificate
rubrics_metrics.description: The supplemental examination certificate lists all items of information properly submitted and states whether an SNQ affecting at least one claim of the patent is raised in the request.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examiners should use the formal 'Supplemental Examination Certificate' form. Examiners should NOT initial, sign, and date the listing of items submitted under 37 CFR 1.610(b)(2); the certificate itself includes citations to each item properly submitted.

rubrics_metrics.name: Content requirements for the Reasons for SNQ Determination (reasons document)
rubrics_metrics.description: The reasons document must explain, for each item of information, why each item does or does not raise an SNQ and identify the claims affected or not affected.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Where an item raises an SNQ, include: (1) a statement that the item raises an SNQ and identification of claims affected; (2) where appropriate, statement that the item does not raise an SNQ and identification of claims not affected; (3) a brief statement of the basis for the determination. Use form paragraph 28.01 as the heading for the reasons document. If an item affects less than all requested claims, identify the claims not affected and provide basis.
